title: WordPress REST error
description: The error body WordPress core produces from a WP_Error, which both custom routes (related and resolve) return for a 400 (a bad argument, such as count out of range or a malformed slug) and a 404 (no such public resource). The shape is core's, not the plugin's: code, message and data.status are always present, and core may add more keys at the top level (additional_errors when a WP_Error carries several codes) and inside data (such as params on a 400), so neither object is closed.

code.description: A machine-readable error code, such as rest_invalid_param, rest_post_invalid_id or resource_hub_not_found.

message.description: A human-readable explanation, translatable and not stable across versions, so the front end branches on code and data.status, not on this.

data.description: The error's data. status mirrors the HTTP status; core adds other keys for some errors, such as params with per-parameter messages on rest_invalid_param.

status.description: The HTTP status the error was sent with: 400 or 404 from the custom routes.
